memory_candidates.content: In BimodalLogic (ProofChecker), a probe written in the Mathlib-only 'all-walks Z-model' idiom (bare formula type, raw relation W -> W -> Prop) ports into the library along one fixed route, and rediscovering it is expensive. The dictionary: the probe's T (fullModel R V) becomes PlusTruthAt M; IsWalk R becomes IsStepPath F at F : FrameOver intOrder; 'every walk' and 'every WorldHistory of a FrameOver intOrder frame' are the SAME set by FrameOver.mem_HF_iff_adjacent, with FrameOver.worldHistoryOfStepPath and WorldHistory.isStepPath as the two directions; the validity target is PlusValidInt on the Z fibre, lifted to PlusValidZTime by plusValidZTime_iff_plusValidInt. Build limit histories with WorldHistory.ofTotal (it wants only forall s t, F.TaskRel (f s) (t - s) (f t)), which is shorter than an adjacency-plus-composition argument. Standing caveat: any argument that needs a marker sequence COFINAL in the duration order is Z-only. A TemporalOrder is an arbitrary nontrivial totally ordered abelian group, so over a dense order a strictly increasing sequence may converge -- such results land at .ZTime, never at .Base, and threading cofinality as an explicit hypothesis on the kernel lemma isolates that dependence at one auditable binder.
